title: Crunchy Crackling Baby Red Potatoes
time_estimate: About 1 hour (boil, cool, then 25-30 mins bake plus more turned over)

ingredients.text: 3 lbs baby red potatoes (2 bags Trader Joe's)
1 ½ tsp kosher salt (add more or less to your preference)
5 garlic cloves; crushed or 5 frozen cubes

steps: Boil potatoes until fork tender in salted water.
Carefully drain. Cool completely, and then cut in half.
Line a REAL metal baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mix together spices, garlic, mayonnaise, and oil.

Add potatoes and toss to coat. Transfer potatoes, cut side down, onto a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 mins. Turn potatoes over (they should be nice and roasted by now) and continue to bake until desired doneness. You can keep the potatoes cut side down longer if you want them darker and crispier.

title: Silan Caramelized onion brisket
time_estimate: About 5½ hours plus cooling and chilling (1–1½ hours caramelizing onions, about 3½ hours baking, then cool completely and refrigerate until firm)

ingredients.text: 3-4 lb second cut brisket or dekel
1/3 cup Heaven n earth date syrup

steps: Preheat the oven to 325°.Pat the brisket/ dekel dry and season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the brisket for 5 minutes per side, until deeply browned. Remove and set aside. Add the remaining oil, onions, and salt to the pot. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring every few minutes, until the onions are deeply golden and caramelized, about 1–1 ½ hours. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and silan. Cook for 2–3 minutes, until the tomato paste darkens. Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer until reduced by half. Stir in the chicken broth, spices and bay leaves.  Return the brisket (and any juices) to the pot, nestling it into the sauce. Cover the pot and transfer to oven.  Bake for about 3 ½ hours, until the brisket is fork-tender. Let the brisket cool completely in the sauce. Remove the meat and refrigerate until firm, then slice against the grain. Return the sliced brisket to the sauce, reheat gently, serve warm with plenty of caramelized onions and sauce spooned over the top.

title: Maple Bourbon Ribs
subtitle: How to Make Amazing Maple Bourbon Back Ribs
description: Back ribs are one of my favorite culinary secrets. They present beautifully and they taste like much more expensive meat. Once you know how to cook them, they’ll be one of your favorite secrets too.
yield_text: Serves: One rack feeds 3-4 meat eaters
time_estimate: About 3½ hours (3 hours covered bake plus prep)
steps: Combine all spice rub ingredients and rub all over the ribs.
Add ribs to a Dutch oven, roasting pan, or baking pan. Add beef stock most of the way up the sides of the ribs. Cover tightly and bake for 3 hours.

clipping_notes.label: To serve
clipping_notes.text: To serve, pour sauce over ribs before rewarming or keep sauce warmish and pour over ribs before serving. Note: Whether you need the broth when rewarming depends on how long you’re going to be rewarming for. If your ribs are basically warm and you’re heating up for just 15-20 minutes, then you can get rid of the broth and pour the sauce over to rewarm. But if you’re going to be rewarming for longer, then it’s best to keep the ribs in the liquid. While it’s fine to pour the sauce over while the ribs are still in the broth, you’ll lose some of the sauce.
